_about: Memory of the visual-polish loop: every correction the user made about how a sheet LOOKS, the rule adopted and where it is encoded. Read it before polishing; append an entry whenever the user (or the lint/PDF) shows a defect not yet covered. Newest last.

lessons.feedback: Neighbour lot titles overlapped; one title was off to the left
lessons.rule: Survey lot notes centred between lot lines, one sheet row shares one X (slope 0.036878), next row = row + half tallest block + 4 ft; straddling note stays centred below

lessons.feedback: Sanitary MH labels were diagonal/crooked and covered the map
lessons.rule: MLeader rotation in RADIANS; text right of the arrow, left-aligned, near-vertical leader

lessons.feedback: Red curved arrows pointing at nothing
lessons.rule: No arrow without a label; blocks with fixed internal colours are hidden, not recoloured

lessons.feedback: EOP / EXIST R/W labels: slanted leaders, text on the left or right at random, text sitting on lines and next to dimensions (screenshots); liked: horizontal leader at the arrow's height with the text outside
lessons.rule: Leaders strictly vertical/horizontal in sheet axes; text right of a vertical leader; labels of one kind and side share one text line; side flips to the left only to avoid survey linework/text; never overlap

lessons.feedback: Wants one fixed visual signature (colours, font, sizes) and a self-improving process
lessons.rule: visual-signature.json is the single source; visual-lint.mjs measures it; this file records corrections; skill + agent civil3d-visual-polish run the loop

lessons.feedback: Screenshots of an 8" G.V. callout and ALIGNMENT START with long diagonal leaders: 'some aesthetic exceptions must be diagonal because the tool cannot know the space and orthogonal would look bad'
lessons.rule: Diagonal leaders are allowed ONLY for multi-line utility callouts and ALIGNMENT START/END; one straight segment, clear space, never crossing text/leaders, one angle family per sheet; EOP / EXIST R/W / SAN MH stay strictly orthogonal
encodedIn: visual-lint.mjs (slant check only on native EOP/RW)

lessons.feedback: Printed overlaps of EXIST R/W text with rotated BLOCK / P.B. survey titles that the model-space lint cannot see
lessons.rule: After lint, verify on the PLOT: road-labels-nudge.mjs reads fase1-qc.py overlap clashes (owners = label handle), pushes the whole row +8 ft further out, repeats until 0 printed overlaps; --dry only reports; --reuse-qc after re-activating the drawing

lessons.feedback: SEIDENSTEIN: R/W marks with diagonal arrows of mixed angle/length, some white and some gray, sparse, missing at the four corners of the SW 74th intersection: 'No me gusta como se ve ese RW... geometricamente estetica'. The user also straightened 3 EOP marks by hand 'para proximas etiquetas'.
lessons.rule: R/W marks follow the EOP signature: leader strictly orthogonal on the SHEET axes, 8 ft long, text beyond the landing (right of a vertical leader), all white, ONE set (survey R/W marks hidden). Station rhythm: 14 ft from every R/W corner on each leg, then equal ~125 ft along every run (survey lines AND the c300-rw-extend.mjs extensions), over the whole plan, not only the sheet frame. A blocked station is retried (street side, farther, tighter, slid <=20 ft, corners <=60 ft) and only omitted when there is no room; marks touching the sheet frame stay fully inside it. Text point offsets are calibrated on the style: landing end = text point +/-(h+0.1) ft inboard and h/2 below.

lessons.source: design engineer (DG), screen recording 2026-10-27 19:25, Seidenstein PROPOSED review
lessons.feedback: Our PROPOSED SAN LAT CONNECTION callouts had been converted from native Civil 3D labels to Multileaders: 'that label is no longer a label, it is a multileader; if I move it the numbers never change; in mine all labels are automatic'. The leaders that used to converge on one point were separated. Also: never change the viewport scale (1"=20' must equal the annotation scale).
lessons.rule: PROPOSED plan callouts with STA/OFF are native Station Offset - Fixed Point labels (style SAN LAT / C.O / WATER SERVICE ...), only the INV text is typed (Edit Label Text); elevations come from native Profile View > Station Elevation labels; the arrow tip is the control point; never explode / convert to MLeader; never change viewport scales; keep the table-linked labels (switch them to no-plot instead of deleting). The orange 'i' override glyph is not a reason to replace a label. The engineer's corrected file is the source of truth: our ideas are suggestions only.
